findings.reason: the plan's only live node must be marked done (or re-scoped to the missing half) before any dispatch, or the first implementation node duplicates a mechanism shipped eight days after this plan was revised.
findings.text: §6's endpoint is already shipped: `reckon/crew/census.py` (354 lines, `census()` and `apply_census()`), the `crew census` command at reckon/crew_run_commands.py:34, tests/test_crew_census.py with 22 test functions, the evidence fragment docs/evidence/fragments/a-crew-process-ends-with-its-owner/crew-census-lists-and-stops-ownerless.html, and commits b9381df2b9, 944f8d0b40 and 568ec13c6c — yet plan-section-declarations still reads `s6: implementable` and the snapshot carries no landed record between §6 and §7. A node dispatched against §6 as written would rebuild landed machinery and re-land the same tests.

findings.reason: the plan's stated mechanism is exactly the missing half, so the brief must carry the launcher write path (dispatch_launch, crew run/complete, producers) or the plan must stop claiming every process carries its owner and say which processes the census can actually see.
findings.text: the ownership stamp §6 makes the foundation of the design has no writer in the product: `RECKON_OWNER_PID` and `RECKON_OWNER_HOST`/`RECKON_OWNER_START_TIME` are read at census.py:141-155 and set nowhere but tests/test_crew_census.py; `RECKON_SESSION_ID` and `RECKON_CREW_SESSION` are read at census.py:138 and set nowhere at all; the only stamp anything writes is `RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER` (reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:566). So §6's claim that "Every process reckon starts carries its owner in its environment … followers, producers, dispatch and complete loops, workers and their review nodes" is unimplemented: such a process falls into `unrecorded_count` (census.py:261) and is never listed, and the done-when "lists zero reckon processes whose owner is dead" passes vacuously for them.

findings.reason: the brief should require revalidation to read the table once for the whole apply (the shape process_signal.py:336 `_beat_marked_processes` already uses), which changes the work the node is asked to do.
findings.text: apply_census takes the report census() produced and then calls census(home=home) again inside its per-pid loop (census.py:318), so N listed orphans cost N full /proc walks plus N ownership resolves; the interface leaks the report shape as a required argument rather than hiding revalidation behind apply itself.

findings.reason: the brief should extend the owner (one table walk with the environment index, one signal path) instead of adding a fifth walk and a second signalling implementation, which is the duplicate the review exists to catch.
findings.text: the shared process-table reader already exists: `_walk_marked_processes` walks /proc once per beat, keys its readings by pid, start tick and executable identity through `_indexed_environment` (process_signal.py:220), and is used by the recovery liveness path. §6's census adds independent walks rather than extending it: reckon/crew/census.py:38 (`_processes`, which also bypasses the shared index by calling the uncached `_process_environment` at census.py:48), reckon/crew/fleet_migrate.py:185, reckon/crew/fleet_migrate.py:488, and reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:4598 (`os.listdir("/proc")`). The signalling half is a second path too: census.py:288-345 implements pidfd open/TERM/KILL escalation with identity revalidation, while reckon/crew/process_signal.py:529 `_signal_one` sends by pid or pgid with no pidfd and no revalidation — the two do the same job and neither knows of the other.

findings.reason: at public_definitions 2541, cli_options 475, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25 the section must account in its own text for the surface it adds, naming what it retires or merging `census --apply`'s stop path with the existing pointer-discard surface.
findings.text: §6 adds `crew census` as a new subcommand with `--apply` and `--pretty` (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:34-45), and its text names nothing it retires, merges, or explains why nothing can be; the section also has the sweep completing stale live pointers where `crew discard` already exists, and does not say whether discard loses surface or is kept beside it.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — census()/apply_census() hide the table walk well, but the split forces the caller to hand the whole report back and apply_census re-walks /proc once per listed pid.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — census.py adds a fourth independent /proc table walk beside the shared one in process_signal.py, and a second signalling path beside process_signal._signal_one.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2541, cli_options 475, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25; §6 adds one subcommand and two options and names nothing it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §6's endpoint already exists as reckon/crew/census.py with a `crew census` CLI command, tests and an evidence fragment, while the plan still declares s6 implementable; and the environment-stamp mechanism §6 depends on has no writer outside census.py and its test.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the new subcommand is a binding over census()/apply_census(), not a second implementation of the resolution; the work behind the interface is real.
